text: Principal component analysis transformed 21 conventional traits into seven independent indexes. Regression analysis selected these indicators: second leaf from the top surface area, peroxidase activity, catalase activity, malondialdehyde content, chlorophyll (a + b), grain weight per ear, and yield.

entities.text: second leaf from the top surface area
entities.label: TRT

text: Key genes TaMAX1, TaMOC1, and TN1 in wheat, ZmTB1, ZmD14, and ZmMOC1 in maize, and MAX1-like genes, OsMAX1, and OsHAM2 in rice are highlighted. In sugarcane, genes SoMAX2, SoMAX3, SoMAX4-1, SoMAX4-2, and SoTB1 regulate bud outgrowth and tillering.

Overexpression of SiCDPK24 in Arabidopsis enhanced drought resistance and improved survival under drought stress. It activated the expressions of stress-related genes RD29A, RD29B, RD22, KIN1, COR15, COR47, LEA14, CBF3/DREB1A, and DREB2A.

QJy-sbi06 was located in a 21.2 kb region on chromosome 6. The candidate gene sobic.006G147400, encoding an NAC transcription factor, was identified in this region. Association analysis and sequencing showed that XL52 has a 1.8 kb transposon insertion in the NAC gene, which interrupts and inactivates the juice yield gene.

A high-density genetic map spanning 2233.5 cM was constructed with 1069 markers. Using 138 reported QTLs, six Meta-QTL regions for heat tolerance were identified. Their confidence interval was reduced by 2.7-folds compared to the reported QTLs.

Water deficit stress affects mung bean growth and reduces yield. A field experiment evaluated four water stress-tolerant genotypes: BARI Mung-8, BMX-08010-2, BMX-010015, and BMX-08009-7, along with two check varieties, BARI Mung-6 and BARI Mung-7, across five environments.

Crown rust resistance is described in oat diploid species A. strigosa accession PI 258731. Resistance from PI 258731 is introgressed into hexaploid A. sativa germplasm. This study maps QTL for resistance in PI 258731. It evaluates the number of QTL. It understands the relationship between the genomic location in A. strigosa and the introgression location in A. sativa. It identifies molecular markers linked with PI 258731 resistance loci. These markers could be used for marker assisted selection and detection of this resistance in diverse A. strigosa accessions.

The study identified morphological and physiological traits associated with drought tolerance in three sorghum varieties: Makueni (MKL) landrace, Gadam (GD) open-pollinated variety, and IESH 22012 hybrid. A randomized split-plot design was used with three sorghum varieties and two moisture levels (control and drought), replicated four times in 2021 and 2022. Rainout shelters imposed drought conditions.

SiCDPK7 transgenic plant lines had higher catalase (CAT) activity and lower malonaldehyde (MDA) content than WT plants. SiCDPK7 transgenic Arabidopsis and foxtail millet showed increased transcription levels of heat and cold stress-responsive genes under stress conditions.

A cowpea genetic map was constructed using the F-2 population from the cross IC-1 x BRS Marataoa, based on SNP markers. The cpi gene was mapped with reference to the species consensus map to identify markers for assisted selection for BNF. Parents and 89 F-2 plants were genotyped with 51,128 SNP markers, and 910 polymorphic markers were used to construct the map.

SbCASP4 improves salt tolerance in sweet sorghum by enhancing the root apoplastic barrier and blocking sodium ion transport to the shoot. Sweet sorghum is a C4 crop tolerant to salt, drought, and waterlogging.

This review focuses on advances in plant protection using CRISPR/Cas9 technology in crops against viral, fungal, and bacterial diseases. For viral disease resistance, strategies in model species like Arabidopsis and Nicotiana benthamiana are discussed. These include integrating CRISPR sequences that target the viral genome and inducing CRISPR-mediated mutations in the host plant genome.
Linkage maps were constructed with SNPs for CT19 X TX430 and ICSV700 X M81 E populations. QTL mapping identified QTL conferring chilling tolerance at seedling stage.
CqGST genes are distributed on all chromosomes except chromosome 09. Chromosome 07 contains 20 CqGST genes. CqGSTL1 and CqGSTU1 cannot be mapped to specific chromosomes.
Over 112,000 SNPs were identified for marker development. 5647 DEGs were identified.
The down-regulation of ribosomal protein-related genes causes stunted growth in salt-sensitive accessions. The salt-tolerant accession alleviates salt stress by increasing energy production.

Quantitative real-time PCR and transcriptional activity assays demonstrated that the gene SiMYB56 activates expression of lignin biosynthesis genes under drought conditions. Overexpression of SiMYB56 leads to ABA accumulation in seeds of transgenic rice plants.

Bioinformatics analysis revealed 186 DEPs related to 37 specific KEGG pathways. Physiological, transcriptome, and proteome analyses demonstrated that maize-peanut intercropping improves photosynthetic characteristics in maize leaves. This improvement is related to PS I, PS II, cytochrome b6f complex, ATP synthase, and photosynthetic CO<sub>2</sub> fixation, caused by improved CO<sub>2</sub> carboxylation efficiency.

Mutagenesis studies showed that the HMA domain is indispensable for Cd binding. Deleting the HMA domain drastically reduced Cd accumulation and impaired yeast growth. Truncating other domains, such as the isoprenylation motif, had no significant effect. SbHIPP40 is a pivotal Cd accumulator via its HMA domain. This advances understanding of sorghum's Cd detoxification mechanisms and offers a genetic resource for enhancing phytoremediation strategies.

SiCBL5 overexpression in foxtail millet increased salt tolerance. SiCBL5 knockdown increased salt hypersensitivity. SiCBL5 physically interacts with SiCIPK24 in vitro and in vivo, shown by yeast two-hybrid and firefly luciferase complementation imaging assays.

The genes of LRNK1 and LR2381 showed different expression patterns under salt stress. Metabolomic data revealed different salicylic acid and betaine profiles between LRNK1 and LR2381, which mediated salt tolerance in sorghum.
The drought-tolerant genotype RTx430 shows a genotype-specific drought response in organelle protein profiles. Its organelle-enriched proteins changed abundance upon drought stress.

We identified candidate genes for salt tolerance in quinoa. Some DEGs were exclusively expressed in the ST genotype. DEGs common to both genotypes under salt stress may be key genes for quinoa salinity adaptation.

Candidate genes include FPA for flowering time (VRADI10G01470; chr. 10), TIR-NBS-LRR for mungbean yellow mosaic India virus resistance (VRADI09G06940; chr. 9), and E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase RIE1 for SPAD value (VRADI07G28100; chr. 7).

18 QTLs were identified for plant height (4 QTLs), fresh weight (8 QTLs), dry weight (3 QTLs), stem diameter (2 QTLs), and sugar content (1 QTL). Two overlapping QTLs, qFW9.2/qDW9 and qFW10/qDW10.2, were detected for fresh weight and dry weight.
SiNF-YC2 interacted with SiCO in the nucleus. SiNF-YC2 promotes flowering and improves resistance to salt stress.

The profiling of 200 Tartary buckwheat accessions shows 540 metabolites were modified by human selection. A metabolic genome-wide association study shows 384 mGWAS signals for 336 metabolites are under selection.

Ten Shaker K+ channel genes were identified in foxtail millet. They were divided into five groups by phylogenetic analysis. Gene structures, chromosome locations, cis-acting regulatory elements in promoters, and post-translation modification sites of the Shaker K+ channels were analyzed.

Overexpression of FtPMEI13 improves drought tolerance by altering antioxidant enzyme activities and osmotically active metabolite levels. FtPMEI13 interacts with pectin methylesterase (PME) and inhibits PME activity under drought stress.

The drought-resistant oat variety DA92-2F6 and the drought-susceptible variety Longyan 3 were investigated under 15% PEG-6000 drought stress. After 7 days of stress, antioxidant enzyme, osmotic adjustment substance, and photosynthetic efficiency were significantly higher in DA92-2F6, except for cell membrane permeability.
15 oat varieties were tested for alkali tolerance under four Na2CO3 treatment levels (0, 10, 20, 40 mM). The alkali tolerance of oat seedlings was evaluated.

Sorghum is sensitive to cold stress in early growth phases. Cold adaptability is crucial for cultivating bioenergy and grain sorghum. Identifying genes that enhance biomass accumulation under early cold stress can improve sorghum varieties.

Plants with drought tolerance QTLs and higher recurrent parent genome were selfed to produce BC4F3. Under non-irrigated conditions, BC4F3 lines with introgressed QTLs had higher yield than both parents.
Ten barley HvASRs were identified, unevenly distributed on three chromosomes. Barley, wheat, Brachypodium distachyon, rice, maize, foxtail millet, and tomato ASRs were classified into two clusters.

SbMYBAS1 (SbMYB119) expression decreased under salt stress. SbMYBAS1 is located in the nucleus. Under salt stress, Arabidopsis plants overexpressing SbMYBAS1 had lower dry/fresh weight and chlorophyll content, and higher membrane permeability, MDA content, and Na+/K+ ratio than wild-type Arabidopsis plants.

Dehydration response element binding proteins (DREBs) are transcriptional regulators that enhance plant tolerance to abiotic stress. This study analyzed the DREB gene family (SiDREBs) in foxtail millet (Setaria italica) using bioinformatics and gene expression under abiotic stress.
SiNP1 encodes a glucose-methanol-choline oxidoreductase. The SiNP1 protein localizes to the endoplasmic reticulum and is expressed in panicle.

Genes were studied for polymorphism among chickpea accessions. One SNP was selected from four identified SNPs between the promoter regions of the two genes. Molecular markers were developed for the SNP and verified using ASQ and CAPS methods.

A half-sib population HZ595 (Hurdal x Z615-4, with 91 lines) was phenotyped in 2011 to validate QTL found in HZ595. Qdon.umb-17A/7C was localized with a phenotypic effect of 12.4%. Three SNPs linked to Qdon.umb-17A/7C were identified in both populations. One SNP each for QTL on 5C, 11A and 13A were identified in HZ595.

SiYTH1 positively regulates drought tolerance in foxtail millet. The siyth1 mutant exhibits reduced stomatal closure and increased H-2 O-2 accumulation under drought stress. SiYTH1 positively regulates transcripts with m(6) A modification related to stomatal closure and ROS scavenging under drought stress.

Cluster analysis classified genotypes into four groups based on grain yield association. Acc. #28546 and Acc. #216739 were highlighted as highly drought tolerant across environments. The study identified 32 QTNs for drought indices and grain yield under stress conditions, and 22 QTNs under non-stress conditions, at two locations. Five common QTNs were linked to multiple drought indices.

Molecular diversity of 40 Tibetan wild barley accessions, 10 Syrian, 72 North American, 36 European, 9 South American, and 8 Australian varieties was characterized using multiple microsatellite loci. The 42 SSR primers amplified 278 alleles across the 175 barley accessions.

Sorghum genes exhibit downregulation in response to drought stress. The review explores drought tolerance in sorghum, including its morphological characteristics, physiological mechanisms, and the identification and selection of its functional genes.

The gene belongs to the S1Fa-like family, is localized in chloroplasts, and lacks transcriptional activation. FtS1Fa1 promotes rutin accumulation in Tartary buckwheat by upregulating the rutin biosynthesis gene.

We identified eight MAPKK and 49 MAPKKK genes in sorghum. We characterized 16 sorghum MAPK genes. RNA-seq analysis revealed that 10 MAPK cascade genes were involved in drought stress response in sorghum.

A QTL (OLRNIII-g864) for lateral root number is near TP3371 and flanked by TP5093 and TP6072 SNP markers. Another QTL (QSRL(IV_61.63)) for specific root length is near TP1873 and flanked by F7XEM6b SRAP and TP1035 SNP markers.

Analysis of cis-acting elements showed that SbPUB genes are involved in response to salt stress. Proteomic and transcriptomic data show that several SbPUB genes have diverse expressions under different salt treatments.

To detect molecular markers linked to the sht1 locus, AFLP analysis was used with bulked segregant analysis of progeny from a cross between a non-brittle common buckwheat and a brittle self-compatible buckwheat line. 312 primer combinations were screened and a linkage map around the sht1 locus was constructed using 102 F-2 plants.
Sheepgrass seedlings survived when soil water content was reduced to 14.09% in a drought stress experiment.

Sorghum (Sorghum bicolor L.) is a drought tolerant staple crop and cold sensitive. Low temperature stresses such as chilling and frost affect the agronomic performance of sorghum and limit its geographical distribution.

A high quality chromosome-scale genome assembly of little millet comprises 18 chromosomes and 59,045 genes. Eleven chromosomes are assembled from telomere to telomere, revealing an 850 Mb tetraploid genome.
The QTL cluster qTN6.2/qFW6/qDW6.1 overlaps with qTN6.1 and qDW6.2. The sorghum ortholog of the heterotic biomass gene ARGOS, Sobic.006G092500, is located within the five QTLs on chromosome 6.

Using 1571 polymorphic SNP markers from the adzuki bean genome, 26 agronomic QTLs and five qualitative trait genes related to pigmentation were mapped via restriction-site-associated DNA sequencing of 150 members of an F2 population from a cross between cultivated and wild adzuki beans. On chromosomes 4, 7, and 10, 11 QTLs for flowering time and pod maturity were mapped. Six QTLs for 100-seed weight were detected.

The new method was applied to a Barley dataset. A QTL can affect multiple traits. The new method increased QTL detection power and found 4 more QTLs than the single-trait method. The -logP values were higher and correlated with single-trait analysis.

To explore genetic diversity of drought-induced oxidative stress tolerance in foxtail millet, lipid peroxidation was used as a biochemical marker to assess membrane integrity under stress. It screened 107 cultivars and classified the genotypes as highly tolerant, tolerant, sensitive, and highly sensitive. Four cultivars with differential dehydration tolerance responses were selected to understand the physiological and biochemical basis of tolerance mechanisms.

AFLP markers clustered on centromeric regions and were more abundant on chromosome 1 (7H). RAPD markers showed 54% segregation distortion, compared to 26% for AFLP markers, 27% for SSR markers, and 18% for RFLP markers.

Tol showed important changes in metabolic pathways during heat shock (GST). These included up-regulation of raffinose family oligosaccharides and down-regulation of the gamma-aminobutyric acid catalytic pathway. Hexose sugar concentration became depleted. Tol tolerated elevated temperatures (ABS) due to up-regulation of osmoprotectants, chaperones, and reactive oxygen species scavengers and by suppression of SnRK1 (GENE) via transcripts and metabolites.

SSR markers and agronomical traits analyzed genetic diversity of 142 sweet sorghum parent lines. The lines were clustered into 5 groups based on agronomical traits. Each group is characterized by morphological traits and main origins.

Seven novel SNPs were identified, including one for HT, one for TN, one for Brix, and four for RS. Candidate genes involved in brassinosteroid regulation, auxin biosynthesis, carbohydrate metabolism, and sugar transport underlie these SNPs.

Quantitative real-time PCR analysis showed SiDREB2 was significantly up-regulated by dehydration (polyethylene glycol) and salinity (NaCl). A synonymous SNP associated with dehydration tolerance was detected at the 558th base pair (an A/G transition) in the SiDREB2 gene in a core set of 45 foxtail millet accessions.

DREB genes code for transcription factors involved in abiotic stress response. Characterizing DREB genes and developing functional markers for effective alleles is important for marker-assisted selection in foxtail millet.
Integrative analyses of transcriptomic data across tissues and developmental stages in sorghum are limited. This limits the discovery of the genetic basis underlying complex agricultural traits.

Six sterile and six restorer lines of sorghum and 36 hybrid sorghum combinations from incomplete double-row crosses were tested. The root bleeding sap of the F1 hybrid sorghum showed high heterosis for soluble sugar content and amino acid content at flowering stage, with average high-parent heterosis of 129.34% and 74.57%, respectively.

Three QTL, QLB-czas1, QLB-czas2, and QLB-czas8, were detected on chromosomes 1, 2, and 8 of Yugu 5. QLB-czas1 explained 14-17% of phenotypic variation in 2 environments. QLB-czas2 explained 9% in 5 environments. QLB-czas8 explained 12-20% in 6 environments. Bulked segregant analysis and RNA sequencing identified common SNPs in the genomic region of QLB-czas8.

Forage sorghum cultivars in India are susceptible to foliar diseases including anthracnose, rust, zonate leaf spot, drechslera leaf blight and target leaf spot. QTLs confer resistance to these foliar diseases.

Traits 1000-grain weight (TGW), grain weight per spike (GWPS), and dry matter content (DMC) exhibited high-parent heterosis, with TGW reaching 82.54%. P-n correlated positively with T-r, C-i, G(s), RuBP carboxylase, PEP carboxylase, GWPS, TGW, and DMC, suggesting T-r, C-i, and G(s) could aid in identifying high-photosynthesis sorghum varieties.

Approximately 60% of the yield potential in foxtail millet breeding over 60 years is attributed to changes in varieties, and approximately 40% to improvements in cultivation measures. The genetic gains in grain yield were 35.79 kg ha-1 year-1 in 2023 and 29.29 kg ha-1 year-1 in 2024. The genetic gain in yield potential was 0.96% YOR-1.

Inhibiting the expression of the FtIST1 gene in Tartary buckwheat by VIGS decreased the activities of antioxidant enzymes SOD, POD, and CAT. It increased plasmalemma permeability and leaf Na+ content. This indicates that loss of FtIST1 gene expression leads to decreased antioxidant capacity, increased cell membrane damage, increased shoot Na+ content, and decreased salt tolerance. FtIST1 is a salt tolerance gene associated with salt tolerance in Tartary buckwheat.

The strip-till fertilizer application depth was 13-15 cm below the soil surface. Corn planted 10 cm from the fertilized row showed greater early season growth, higher plant population, and higher grain yield.

NPBTs have been applied to address pathogen threats in citrus. Citrus could use NPBTs due to its complex biology, including seedlessness, apomixis, high heterozygosity, long juvenility, and aptitude for in vitro manipulation.
ABA treatment depressed most FtRCARs transcripts. ABA upregulated CHS, CHI, F3'H, F3H and FLS transcripts, while 4CL and PAL transcripts were down-regulated.

The anthracnose resistance in sorghum line SC112-14 (Cs-SC112) was studied using F2 progenies and recombinant inbred lines against pathotypes from Puerto Rico, Texas, Arkansas, and Georgia. The results show that a series of nearest single loci at the distal region of chromosome 5 control the resistance against pathotypes from Puerto Rico, Texas, and Arkansas.

AP2/ERF genes in Arabidopsis, wheat, rice and barley are extensively studied. In quinoa, AP2/ERF genes lacked systematic investigation. This study identified and characterized AP2/ERF genes in quinoa genome-wide. 105 CqAP2/ERF genes were identified. Phylogenetic analysis classified them into 5 subfamilies.

Expression profiling showed tissue-specific patterns: preferential expression in roots (12 genes), stems (6 genes), leaves (5 genes), and spikes (7 genes). Three genes showed dual peak expression in stems and leaves. Under salt and drought stress, AsEPF/EPFLs are induced, with different genes showing varying expression patterns.
We identified an elite haplotype Hap2 of SiNLP2, which is utilized in breeding. Our study provided gene resources for variety improvement and marker-assisted selection.
The qSL2-5 overlaps with the zeo1 gene. zeo1 is the SL regulatory gene in qSL2-5. The qSRN2-1 overlaps with vrs1. vrs1 affects SRN.
Nucleoredoxin (NRX) is a member of the thioredoxin (TRX) superfamily. It regulates plant growth, development, and stress responses. Its role in drought resistance in foxtail millet is unclear.

Transcriptome profiling and qPCR validation in the YuGu 56 cultivar identified stress-responsive candidates SiC2H2-35 and SiC2H2-58 for salt tolerance, and SiC2H2-23 with 5.19-fold induction under salt stress and SiC2H2-32 with 5.47-fold induction under drought. This study provides insights into the C2H2-ZFP family in foxtail millet and highlights potential genetic markers for improving stress resilience through molecular breeding.

Tolerant accession Q68 showed superior salt tolerance associated with faster root-specific H2O2 accumulation and reactive oxygen species-induced K+ and Ca2+ fluxes in the root apex within 30 min after NaCl application. This was associated with constitutive up-regulation of membrane-localized receptor kinase regulatory protein FERONIA.

SbMYC2 directly activates the expression of the GLUTATHIONE-DISULFIDE REDUCTASE gene SbGR1. SbGR1 silencing weakened drought tolerance in sorghum, and increased ROS accumulation and decreased chlorophyll content in sorghum leaves.

In the germination stage, SbNAC56 overexpression transgenic lines exhibited enhanced hypersensitivities to ABA, NaCl and d-Mannitol. This indicates SbNAC56 plays roles in plant response to abiotic stresses in an ABA dependent signaling pathway.

Seed dormancy is a key domestication trait for major crops. It is acquired in long-term development processes and enables plant survival in adverse conditions. Seed dormancy is a complex trait under polygenic control and is affected by endogenous and environmental factors.

Pc39 cosegregated with SNP marker GMI_ES01_c12570_390 in the AC Assiniboia/MN841801 RIL population. It was flanked by SNP markers avgbs_126086.1.41 and GMI_ES15_c276_702, with genetic distances of 1.7 and 0.3 cM, respectively. In the AC Medallion/MN841801 RIL population, similar results were obtained. The flanking markers had genetic distances of 0.4 and 0.4 cM, respectively.

Foliar resistance to Ascochyta lentis is controlled by a dominant gene (AbR(1)) in lentil accession ILL5588 ('Northfield'). Flanking RAPD markers linked to the resistance locus were identified by bulked segregant analysis.

Maize-peanut intercropping enhanced carbon fixation and carboxylation in maize leaves compared to maize monocropping. In intercropping, apparent quantum yield (AQY), light-saturated net photosynthetic rate (LSPn), light saturation point (LSP), and light compensation point (LCP) increased by 11.6%, 9.4%, 8.9%, and 32.1%, respectively. Carboxylation efficiency (CE), CO2 saturation point (Cisat), Rubisco maximum carboxylation rate (Vcmax), maximum electron transfer rate (Jmax), and triose phosphate utilization rate (TPU) increased by 28.5%, 7.3%, 18.7%, 29.2%, and 17.0%, respectively. The CO2 compensation point (Γ) decreased by 22.6%.

Yield was positively correlated with the number of effective branches, main panicle length, and 1000-grain weight. Path analysis indicated that MDA content, proline content, CAT activity, and soluble sugar content positively affected yield.

Leaf width correlated with plant-level transpiration efficiency and associated with 19 QTL in sorghum. Reducing transpiration without compromising photosynthesis and yield enhances plant transpiration efficiency, a desirable selection target in crop improvement.

Salt-tolerant cultivars maintained higher growth rate, leaf cell membrane integrity, and osmotic adjustment capability under saline condition by enhancing antioxidant enzyme activities and accumulating osmotic regulators. Compared to salt-sensitive cultivars, salt-tolerant cultivars reduced root Na+ uptake by decreasing AsAKT1 and AsHKT2;1 expression, excluded more root Na+ by increasing AsSOS1 expression, compartmentalized more Na+ into root vacuoles by increasing AsNHX1 and AsVATP-P1 expression, and absorbed more K+ by increasing AsKUP1 expression.

Single-marker analysis and composite interval mapping identified a QTL on chromosome 5 associated with egg number and egg number per gram of root from the resistant sweet sorghum line PI 144134. This QTL on chromosome 5 and a prior QTL on chromosome 3 can be moved from PI 144134 and Honey Drip, respectively, into elite sorghum germplasm via marker-assisted selection.

text: Lodging reduces grain yield in cereal crops. Stem height, diameter, and strength are crucial for lodging resistance, grain yield, and photosynthate transport in barley. Understanding the genetic basis of stem benefits barley breeding.

Sorghum bicolor is a tolerant cereal crop. C2 domain family proteins are involved in the response to abiotic stress such as salt and drought stress. Less information on C2 domain family members has been reported in Sorghum bicolor.

Two major-effect QTLs SCot8-B-CAAT5-D and HVM54-Bmag0571 on chromosomes 1 and 2 have positive allele effects for developing barley varieties for drought conditions. The new alleles qLWS-4a, qSLS-4, qLNS-7b, qSCS-7, and qLNS-7a are useful for pyramiding elite alleles in molecular breeding and marker assisted selection to improve salinity tolerance in barley.

To isolate the gene, a high-resolution mapping population with 10,204 meiotic events was constructed. F-2 plants were screened using co-dominant flanking markers, and segmental recombinant inbred lines (RILs) were tested for BaMMV resistance.

The study dissected resistance into QTL using phenotypic data from four environments and a 162 microsatellite marker linkage map from 168 RILs of cross 296B x IS18551. For five component traits across four environments, 29 QTL were detected by multiple QTL mapping: four for leaf glossiness, four for seedling vigor, seven for oviposition, six for deadhearts, two for adaxial trichome density, and six for abaxial trichome density.

We identified 217 foxtail millet seed resources for drought resistance at the maturity stage. Two cultivars with extremely strong drought resistance, JKH4 (Chi 5422) and JKH6 (Chigu 26), and two with extremely weak drought resistance, JRK3 (17M1309) and JRK6 (Canggu 9), were selected for physiological comparison and transcriptome sequencing before and after drought treatment.
Map-based cloning showed an eight-base pair deletion in the sixth exon of wp1.a in LOC101786849, causing premature termination. WP1 encodes phytoene synthase.
Citric acid treatment up-regulated CHS, ANR, MYB and bHLH genes and promoted flavonoid accumulation. It delayed sorghum seed discoloration and enhanced antioxidant activity and storage life.

We constructed 36 transcriptome libraries from four sorghum materials with contrasting germination abilities at three developmental stages. KEGG analysis showed enrichment in metabolic pathways, biosynthesis of secondary metabolites, starch and sucrose metabolism, and plant hormone signal transduction.
Twenty-six SNP markers were significantly associated with starch content. These SNP markers were located on chromosomes 1H and 4H, and were loci of qSC1-1 and qSC4-1, respectively.

A recombinant inbred line (RIL) population of 189 individuals was derived from a cross between the sweet sorghum cultivar 'Rio' and the grain sorghum 'BTx623'. Plant height, Brix, 100-grain weight, and flowering time were evaluated over 3 years.
Foxtail millet is a drought-resistant crop. Its drought resistance mechanism is not fully understood. N-6-methyladenosine modification affects plant growth and stress responses.
SbPLD beta 1 is the target gene of sbi-miR159. SbPLD delta 2 is the target gene of sbi-miR167.
A GWAS involved 446 elite oat (Avena sativa L.) breeding lines from North America. They were genotyped with 1005 DArT markers and had phenotypic data from historical and balanced 2-year data.

We identified 70 B3 proteins in pearl millet and categorized them into ARF, RAV, LAV, and REM subfamilies. We mapped their chromosomal locations and analyzed their gene structures, conserved motifs, and gene duplication events.

Many MQTL were located on chromosomes 2H and 5H. Chromosome 2H was mainly for water-logging and drought. Chromosome 5H was mainly for salinity and low temperature. Chromosomes 2H and 5H are important for barley abiotic tolerance. Genes associated with abiotic stresses are concentrated on these chromosomes.

SNP loci linked to the crown rust resistance gene Pc98 were identified. KASP assays were developed for marker-assisted selection. Crown rust is a damaging disease of oat caused by Puccinia coronata var. avenae f. sp. avenae.

text: GsNAC2-overexpressing sorghum had lower H2O2 and O-2(-) levels, plasma membrane relative permeability, and malondialdehyde (MDA) content. Transcriptome analysis showed a high proportion of differentially-expressed genes (DEGs) participated in defence mechanisms. 18 DEGs were related to synthetic glutathione.
The SiARDP gene was cloned from foxtail millet. Its transcript level increased after drought, high salt, low temperature, and ABA treatment in foxtail millet seedlings.
The drought resistant hybrid M79 and its parental lines E1 and H1 were exposed to drought stress. M79 showed higher photosynthetic energy conversion efficiency and drought tolerance than E1 and H1.

A barley mapping population was developed using morphological marker stocks as parents. Ninety-four doubled-haploid lines were derived from an F-1 using the Hordeum bulbosum system for genetic mapping.
Genes regulating chlorophyll content (CC) and relative water content (RWC) under abiotic stress were screened using WGCNA. Gene-trait correlations were defined as modules, each denoted by a color.

Sheepgrass adapts to adverse environments including cold, salinity, alkalinity and drought. It can survive with soil moisture below 6% in dry seasons. Little is known about sheepgrass water stress tolerance at the molecular level.

The study introduced Populus euphratica PeNAC1 into hexaploid cultivated oat, producing six transgenic lines. Under salt stress, PeNAC1 expression improved seed germination rate, seedling survival rate, and leaf chlorophyll content in transgenic plants compared to the non-transgenic control. These changes increased spikelet number and grain number per spike in transgenic oat under salinity and reduced yield loss per plant.

Two QTL on chromosomes 5H and 6H, designated Qcl.caf-5H and Qcl.caf-6H, are novel. Qcl.caf-5H explained up to 30.9% of phenotypic variance with a LOD of 15.1. Five near isogenic line pairs were developed to validate this QTL. The NILs showed an average 21.0% difference in CL.

Genome-wide association analysis detected four markers highly associated with hullessness. Three were mapped on linkage group Mrg21 between 195.7 and 212.1 cM, indicating the dominantN1 locus on Mrg21 is the major factor controlling this trait.
RT-qPCR verified the transcriptome data. Inhibiting SiPME67 expression with antisense Oligonucleotide caused abnormal pollen tube subapical growth.
Two statistical models, MLM and BLINK, identified 44 shared SNPs. Notable candidate genes include FPA for flowering time (VRADI10G01470; chr.
Broomcorn millet (Panicum miliaceum L.) is adapted to drought, heat, and salinity. Genes involved in these processes can improve the crop.

Establishing gene function is essential for improving sorghum. Identifying genes associated with abiotic stress tolerances in sorghum requires molecular understanding. Over 40% of the sorghum transcriptome was not annotated.

A drought tolerance QTL on chromosome 2 was transferred from barley cultivar 'Tadmor' to cultivars 'Baronesse' and 'Aydanhanim'. The QTL's effects on drought tolerance and other traits were studied using near-isogenic lines in controlled environments and field trials.

Mutations in the Phytochrome C (SiPHYC) gene, including transposon insertions and a frame shift mutation, cause the extremely early heading phenotype. RNA-Seq analysis identified 19 differentially expressed genes associated with this phenotype. Genome-wide InDels and SNPs were identified, providing resources for marker-assisted breeding.

The agronomic performance and chromosome behavior of autotetraploid sorghum inbreds and F1 hybrids were investigated. Autotetraploids have commercial use and can serve as bridging species in crosses to natural tetraploids.

Transcriptome and metabolite analyses identified 652 differentially expressed genes and 571 differentially expressed metabolites in FA-treated oat leaves under drought stress. These genes and metabolites are involved in phenylpropanoid biosynthesis and glutathione metabolism pathways.
Pearl millet is tolerant to heat and drought. It can be used to identify heat-resistant genes.
Foxtail millet (Setaria italica) has high tolerance to drought stress. The SNARE gene is related to drought stress in foxtail millet.

CcCIPK14 was used as bait in a yeast two-hybrid screen. CcCBL1 was identified as an interactor. In vitro, CcCIPK14 exhibited autophosphorylation and phosphorylation of CcCBL1. Plants overexpressing CcCBL1 showed higher survival rates under drought stress. They also exhibited higher expression of flavonoid biosynthetic genes and higher flavonoid content.

Droughts negatively affect sorghum's productivity and nutritional quality. However, resilient genotypes exist across its diversity centers. These genotypes function differently under drought stress at molecular and physiological levels.

Quinoa is an economic crop. Drought affects quinoa yield. Clarifying quinoa adaptation to drought is conducive to cultivating drought-tolerant varieties. The study of quinoa drought stress-related metabolism and identification of related metabolites are unknown.

The salt-tolerant cultivar Vao-9 enhances carbohydrate and energy metabolism through the pentose and glucuronate interconversions and carbon fixation pathways in prokaryotes, reducing salt stress damage. Down-regulation of ribosomes and up-regulated expression of HSPs and CRT occur through the regulation of protein synthesis in response to salt stress.

FtMYB30 overexpression under drought and salt stress reduced oxidative damage in transgenic plants by increasing proline content and antioxidant enzyme activity, and upregulated RD29A, RD29B, and Cu/ZnSOD expression, enhancing drought/salt tolerance. FtMYB30 overexpression also reduced ABA sensitivity in transgenic plants.

Major QTLs for heading date, plant height, node number, stem diameter, panicle neck length, and flag leaf width were consistently detected under both photoperiods. Close associations of genomic regions on chromosomes 6 and 7 with multiple traits suggest pleiotropy or tight linkage.

Analysis revealed that quinoa inhibits photosynthesis at high temperatures. Strategies for high temperature stress management include regulation of heat stress transcription factors (HSFs) for heat tolerance and regulation of purine metabolism to enhance stress signals. The tolerant genotype may have an enhanced response through lower purine levels.

SiDREBs were identified as 166 family members and classified into six subfamilies. They are unevenly distributed on nine chromosomes and designated as SiDREB1-166 based on their chromosomal positions.

The expression levels of three SWEET genes and four PIP genes were higher in YG than in An. This allocated more photosynthetic sugar to the roots. The high expression levels of SiPIPs enhanced root water transport capacity.

The grain number determination in sorghum was studied based on crop growth rate around flowering, reproductive biomass partitioning to the panicle, and grain-set efficiency per unit of panicle biomass. P-R and E-G are genotype-specific traits.

entities.text: reproductive biomass partitioning to the panicle
entities.label: TRT

text: Hexaploid amphiploids have the AACCDD genome composition, while octoploid amphiploids have AACCCCDD, AAAACCDD, or AABBCCDD compositions. The A, B, C, and D oat genomes differ in involvement in non-centromeric, intercalary translocations.
Six PCR-based markers were developed to identify the resistant Pc39 allele. The closely linked marker SCAR_3456624 is within 0.37 cM of Pc39.

The genetic structure of 142 sorghum parent lines was analyzed using a model-based approach with SSR markers. Forty-one SSR markers were selected from 103 markers. These markers generated 189 alleles, ranging from 2 to 11 per marker, with an average of 4.6.

Jingu 21 resistance to 31 herbicides was categorized into five levels: extremely weak, weak, moderate, strong, and extremely strong. Jingu 21 showed extremely strong resistance to lactofen, butachlor, and anilofos.

Foxtail millet (Setaria italica) is a crop with salt and drought tolerance. 16 PLATZ genes are identified in foxtail millet. These genes are mainly expressed in roots and panicles and are induced by abiotic stresses.
SiASR4 expression increased in SiARDP-overexpressing plants. SiASR4-transgenic Arabidopsis and SiASR4-overexpressing foxtail millet showed enhanced tolerance to drought and salt stress.

Association analysis identified 38 significant marker-trait associations under GLM and 31 under MLM. Five markers were associated with crude protein content, three with beta-glucan content, and seven with yield traits.

Four mungbean F-5 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) from crosses of two wild types (ACC 1, ACC 87) and two cultivars (Berken, Kiloga) were used with DArT markers to construct linkage maps and identify QTLs associated with 54 traits. Polymorphic DArT markers varied from 1062 to 2013 among the four RIL populations.

The ASM was validated in 170 foxtail millet accessions using single-marker regression analysis. Regression of lipid peroxidation (LP) on the ASM showed that the SiDREB2-associated trait explained 27.18% of LP variation, indicating it is a major QTL for dehydration tolerance.

Some domestication- and improvement-related genes involved in stress resistance lost functions or reduced expression levels due to trade-offs between stress resistance and productivity. This study provided novel genetic materials for molecular breeding of broomcorn millet varieties with improved agronomic traits.

Expression analysis showed that FeRDEB1 gene transcript levels increased rapidly after low-/high-temperature treatment, drought stress, and exogenous ABA treatment. Over-expression of FeDREB1 gene enhanced drought and freezing tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis but caused growth retardation.
42 common unigenes expressed differentially in all four cultivars after 100 mM NaCl for 48 h. These DEGs may be involved in salinity response. Eight of the 42 DEGs encode transcription factors.

T2 transgenic 35S:VrNHX1 lines maintained a higher K+/Na+ ratio in aerial parts under salt stress and accumulated higher [Na+] in roots than wild-type. They had lower lipid peroxidation, hydrogen peroxide and oxygen radical production, but higher relative water content and proline, ascorbate and chlorophyll contents.

Differentially expressed proteins unique to JK3 were enriched in metabolic pathways. Integrated proteomic and transcriptomic analysis revealed 17 co-upregulated differentially expressed genes exclusive to JK3.
Two minor QTLs (qBX3.1 and qBX7.1) for Brix (BX) were mapped on chromosomes 3 and 7. The QTLs in two clusters (qPH7.1/qBX7.1 and qPH7.1/qFBW7.1) overlapped for PH, FBW and BX.

Fifteen QTLs were related to NUE and its components. Most QTLs were detected at lower nitrogen rates, none at the highest rate. These QTLs were found on Chromosomes 3(3H) and 7(5H) in 2005 and on Chromosome 2(2H) in 2008.
Waxy sorghum seeds have reduced amylose content in starch. A nonfunctional waxy (wx) allele causes waxy endosperms by the absence of granule-bound starch synthase enzyme in sorghum.

Perenniality was introduced from S. halepense into S. bicolor. QTL affecting eight seed yield-related traits and their linkage relationships were identified. Interval mapping in the BC1F2 population from S. bicolor x S. halepense revealed 80 QTL with LOD > 2.5 for the eight traits, ranging from 1 to 13 QTL per trait.

The R2R3-MYB transcription factor FtMYB43 positively regulates procyanidin synthesis. The glycoside hydrolase gene FtSAGH1 is responsible for releasing active salicylic acid, which is a precursor of aspirin and is involved in plant defence.
In Tartary buckwheat, 12 ABA receptors were identified, designated as FtRCAR1 through FtRCAR12. FtRCARs are divided into three subfamily.
SiLTP ectopic expression in tobacco increased salt and drought tolerance compared to the wild type (WT). SiLTP overexpression (OE) and RNA interference (RNAi) transgenic foxtail millet were obtained.
An F-2 population was generated from a cross between sweet sorghum cv. 'Erdurmus' and grain sorghum cv. 'Ogretmenoglu'. A genetic map was constructed from SNPs discovered by ddRAD-seq.

A genome-wide association study identified SNP site Ft4:1777524 as associated with rutin levels. In the 400 kb candidate region, 27 key genes were identified. Transcriptome analysis revealed that FtS1Fa1 is linked to RC.
SbPUB genes are unevenly distributed on the 10 chromosomes of sorghum. Most SbPUB genes (16) are on chromosome 4. No SbPUB genes are on chromosome 5.

An F-2 population was derived from a cross between the breeding line 'Tokei1121' (T1121) and the cultivar 'Erimo167'. It was phenotyped for epicotyl length (ECL) and genotyped using SSR and SNP markers. A molecular linkage map was generated. Fifty-two segregating markers, including 27 SSRs and 25 SNPs, were located on seven linkage groups at a LOD threshold of 3.0.
Under drought conditions, root length increased significantly for both varieties ('Zhonggu2' > 'An04'). K+, Ca2+ and NO3- content increased significantly in Zhonggu2.

A core collection of 888 foxtail millet accessions was inoculated with blast strain HN-1. GWAS identified regulators for blast disease resistance. Phenotypic variation showed: <1.60% highly resistant, 35.25% moderately resistant, 57.09% moderately susceptible, 6.08% highly susceptible.

Nineteen genes for anthocyanin biosynthesis were annotated in this genomic region. Gene Si1g06530 encodes a SANT/Myb domain protein and was highly expressed in developing panicles and seeds. It is a candidate gene for the brown hull color of Jigu 31.

The salt tolerance of 188 accessions was evaluated using shoot length, root length, shoot fresh weight, root fresh weight, shoot dry weight, and root dry weight. The evaluation used the salt tolerant index, Spearman correlation analysis, membership function analysis, principal component analysis, and cluster analysis. The results classified the accessions as highly salt tolerant, salt-tolerant, moderate, salt-sensitive, or highly salt-sensitive.

QTLs for height of the tallest basal tiller, number of basal tillers per plant, panicle length, leaf angle, maturity, and awn length were mapped. Three or more QTLs were mapped in linkage groups A, E, G, and I. No QTLs were mapped in linkage groups B and D.

text: The MTSI selection index selected genotypes based on multiple agro-morphological traits, excluding leaf-to-stem ratio. Genotypes G81, G90, G80, and G89 were identified as desirable by MTSI.

A set of 103 recombinant inbred line (RIL) populations from the Badia and Kavir cross was evaluated under normal, salinity, and drought conditions in 2019. Linkage maps were prepared using 152 SSR markers, 72 ISSR, 7 IRAP, 29 CAAT, 27 SCoT, and 15 iPBS alleles.

Tan1 and Tan2 play a major role in seed dormancy and induce resistance against soil-borne pathogens under cold and wet soil conditions. Seed tannin content may be used as an indirect selection marker for identifying cold tolerant germplasm for breeding.

SbERF027-overexpressing lines had higher cold tolerance than wild-type plants. SbERF027-silenced lines via VIGS had lower cold tolerance than wild-type plants. SNP-911 of the promoter enhanced cold tolerance by mediating SbERF027 expression.

Comparative genomics and QTL analysis revealed the genetic basis of the easily dehulled trait in a particular variety. This variety was artificially selected by the Wa people, who cultivate Tartary buckwheat as a staple food to prevent lysine deficiency.
Salinity did not affect the leaf and root dry weight of Baiyan2. The leaf and root dry weight of Mengnongda1 were reduced by 42% and 35%, respectively.
Triploid Miscanthus × giganteus is a sterile perennial grass used for biomass production. A scale standardizing description of M. × giganteus morphological stages has not been developed.
312 significant MTAs were identified, with 70 MTAs for 100-seed weight. 18 SNPs from 5 genes (ERECTA, ASR, DREB, CAP2 promoter, AMDH) were associated with traits.
GWAS identified 77 SNPs associated with waterlogging tolerance during germination. RNA-Seq revealed 1776 DEGs in Liu Leng Zi Da Mai (tolerant) and 839 DEGs in Naso Nijo (sensitive).

LN improved the expression of flavonoid biosynthetic genes. The transcriptional regulation mediated by MYB and bHLH was analyzed. 78 transcription factors, 124 small secreted peptides and 38 receptor-like protein kinases encoding genes were involved in LN response.

It is tolerant to drought, salinity, and high temperature. To understand salinity tolerance mechanisms, physiological and transcriptome analyses were conducted between salinity tolerant line ICMB 01222 and salinity susceptible line ICMB 081 under control and salinity conditions.

A recombinant inbred line population derived from a cross between DZZ and KL10 was developed. A high-density genetic map was constructed using genotyping-by-sequencing data, and QTL analysis was performed across five environments.
Under high temperature stress, FtPYL16 expression dropped to 0.12 and FtPYL17 fell to 0.22. At grain development stages, FtPY15 expression is high at 19 D.
A single recessive gene from T1121 contributes to longer ECL. Using five insertion and deletion markers, the gene was fine mapped to a ~255 kb region near LG10.

FtNAC31 overexpression lines had sharply increased superoxide dismutase, peroxidase, and catalase activities under stresses. The expression of RD29A, RD29B, RD22, DREB2B, NCED3, and POD1 was dramatically upregulated.

A core set of 96 diverse common bean genotypes was characterized using 91 genome-wide genomic and genic SSR markers. The study identified 691 alleles ranging from 2 to 21 with an average of 7.59 alleles per locus. This effort aimed to identify genes and QTLs for yield and yield-contributing traits.
SiPRR37 expression changes resulted from a Tc1-Mariner transposon insertion in its first intron. SiPRR37 contributed to adaptation in northeastern ecoregions.

The Agrobacterium-mediated transformation protocol was optimised for F. tataricum callus, achieving a transformation rate of approximately 20%. The protocol was confirmed by successful GUS staining, GFP expression, and albino plant generation via FtPDS gene inactivation.

The Milletdb database contains GWAS results for 20 yield-related traits. These traits were measured under three environmental conditions: field (no stress), early drought, and late drought over two years.

A genome-wide association study (GWAS) used 132 mungbean genotypes for traits including flowering time, YMD resistance, SPAD value, trichome density, and leaf area. Genotyping by sequencing (GBS) identified 31,953 high-quality SNPs across all 11 mungbean chromosomes for the GWAS.

122 doubled haploid lines from a cross between cultivars Huaai 11 and Huadamai 6 were genotyped by 9680 SNPs and phenotyped for 14 agronomic traits. 913 quantitative trait nucleotides (QTNs) were identified by five multi-locus GWAS methods to be associated with the 14 traits.

Pc39 is a major race-specific crown rust resistance gene found in an Israeli accession of the wild hexaploid Avena sterilis. Its effectiveness in Europe has decreased but remains relatively high. Molecular markers would aid its mapping and deployment in breeding programs.

This study constructed recombinant inbred lines (RILs) using cultivated species and wild buckwheat. 84,521 SNP markers were identified by Genotyping-by-Sequencing (GBS). High-resolution, high-density SNP genetic maps were developed for QTL mapping, gene cloning and comparative mapping of buckwheat.

Loss-of-function mutations in CCD7, CCD8, MAX1, and DUF genes downregulated expression of associated genes in the SL biosynthetic pathway. Edited lines showed phenotypic changes compared to wild-type plants.

qRT-PCR analysis indicated that multiple stress-responsive genes expression in transgenic lines was significantly higher than in WT under drought stress. The expression of AtNCED gene in ABA biosynthesis was increased significantly under normal and stress conditions. An ABA-response-element (ABRE) was found in promoter regions.
AsA priming enhanced seed vigor in aged oat (Avena sativa) seeds. The seeds were aged by controlled deterioration at 45 degrees C for 5 days and primed with 1.5 mM AsA for 24 h.

LCR4 exhibited robust resistance against stripe rust infection at both the seedling stage and the adult stage upon inoculation with Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Pst) race V26 and mixed Pst races, respectively. Genetic analysis elucidated that the translocated 2RL chromosome segment is responsible for this resistance.
EBR application up-regulated CqBIN2 transcript levels and proline biosynthesis genes. Silencing CqBIN2 by VIGS reduced drought tolerance, survival rate, and proline content in quinoa seedlings.

QTL VaSdt4.1 for seed thickness (SDT) and three QTLs for branch number on the main stem were detected on chromosome 4. QTLs for maximum leaf width (LFMW) and stem internode length were mapped to chromosomes 2 and 9. Genes controlling seed coat, pod, stem and flower color were mapped to chromosomes 3 and 1.

Digital RNA sequence analysis indicated that ST 47 maintained better Na+ and K+ homeostasis by coordinated regulation of transporter genes. The abundance of transcripts involved in chlorophyll metabolism and photosynthesis pathways was higher in ST 47 than in SS 212, which contributed to biomass accumulation. ST 47 resists Na+ toxicity via coordinated physiological, morphological, and molecular mechanisms.

DNA marker GSR345 is a reliable diagnostic tool for greenbug resistance in twenty sorghum accessions. It facilitates marker-assisted breeding for aphid resistance and positional-cloning of SgR1 in sorghum.

Functional genomics techniques have enabled the identification of key genes implicated in defense responses against fungal pathogens in sorghum. Genome editing of identified resistance genes holds promise for developing high-performing varieties.

Expression profiling of NILs and qRT-PCR assays showed changes in predicted genes at 30 and 45 DAF in leaf tissues of qSTG introgressed lines. There was a significant difference in transcript levels of genes between different DAF. QTL pyramiding has potential for improving plant performance under adverse environmental conditions.
Sorghum seedlings with silenced SbNAC9 showed weakened drought stress tolerance. SbNAC9 directly activates the peroxidase gene SbC5YQ75 and the ABA biosynthesis gene SbNCED3.
FtMYB30 is an R2R3-MYB transcription factor from the SG22 family. It localizes in the nucleus and has transcriptional activation activity. FtMYB30 responds to abiotic stress and abscisic acid (ABA).
